settings.retentionHint: The scheduler brings questions back just before you would forget them. Aiming higher means remembering more, but reviews grow quickly: 95% needs about twice as many as 90%.

endgames.intro: Basic endgames against the engine at full strength. It defends as well as it can, so a won drill is really won.
endgames.name.kp-sixth: King on the sixth: promote the pawn
endgames.name.kp-hold: Hold the draw against a pawn
endgames.goal.promote: promote the pawn within {n} moves, and keep the new queen.
endgames.tip.kq-k: Use the queen to shrink the king's box a knight's move away, then bring your own king. Watch out for stalemate.
endgames.tip.krr-k: The rooks take turns: one cuts off a rank, the other checks on the next. Keep them away from the king.
endgames.tip.kr-k: Cut the king off with the rook, bring your king opposite theirs, then check. Push the box smaller step by step.
endgames.tip.kp-sixth: With your king on the sixth rank in front of the pawn, the pawn always gets through.
endgames.tip.kp-opposition: Walk your king in front of the pawn first. Take the opposition: kings face each other with one square between, and the other side must move.
endgames.tip.kp-hold: Stay in front of the pawn. When the kings face each other, make sure it is White who has to move.
endgames.tip.kbb-k: The bishops side by side build a wall. Drive the king into a corner with help from your king.
endgames.tip.lucena: Bring your rook to the fourth rank first, then use it as a bridge to block the checks.
endgames.tip.philidor: Keep your rook on your sixth rank until the pawn moves forward, then check from behind.
endgames.tip.kbn-k: The hardest basic mate: drive the king to a corner of your bishop's colour. Knight and bishop work as a team.

drill.ohm.U: A resistor of **{r}** carries **{i}**. What is the voltage across it?
drill.ohm.I: There are **{u}** across a resistor of **{r}**. What current flows?
drill.ohm.R: There are **{u}** across a resistor and **{i}** flows. How large is the resistance?
drill.quadratic.p: Solve. Give every solution, separated by a comma.
drill.line.m: A straight line goes through these two points. What is its slope m?
drill.line.b: A straight line goes through these two points. Where does it cross the y-axis (b in y = mx + b)?
drill.s.placeValues: Each place is worth twice the place to its right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, ... Add the values where there is a 1.
drill.s.divideBy: Divide by {d} again and again and write down the remainders.
drill.s.readUp: Read the remainders from the bottom up: **{answer}**
drill.s.hexDigits: Hex digits go 0-9, then A = 10, B = 11, C = 12, D = 13, E = 14, F = 15.
drill.s.hexPlaces: Each place is worth 16 times the place to its right: 1, 16, 256, 4096. Multiply and add.
drill.s.nibbles: Split the bits into groups of four from the right and turn each group into one hex digit.
drill.s.nibblesBack: Turn each hex digit into a group of four bits.
drill.s.unitDecimal: Units with k, M, G, T without the i step by a factor of {factor}.
drill.s.unitBinary: Units with i (KiB, MiB, GiB) step by a factor of 1024.
drill.s.unitGiB: 1 GB is 1000³ bytes, 1 GiB is 1024³ bytes. Go through bytes.
drill.s.unitUp: From {from} to the smaller unit {to}: multiply.
drill.s.unitDown: From {from} to the larger unit {to}: divide.
drill.s.toBits: Speeds are in bits per second, so turn the size into bits first (× 8).
drill.s.ones: /{prefix} means {prefix} ones from the left, then zeros:
drill.s.octets: Turn each group of 8 bits into a number (11111111 = 255).
drill.s.hostBits: {prefix} bits are the network, so 32 − {prefix} = {h} bits are left for hosts.
drill.s.minus2: The first address (the network) and the last (broadcast) can't be used by a device.
drill.s.interesting: Octet {n} is the one that is neither 255 nor 0: {octet}.
drill.s.blockSize: So networks come in blocks of **{block}**. Find the block the address falls in:
drill.s.netRest: Octets before it stay the same, octets after it become 0.
drill.s.bcLast: The block runs from {from} to {to}; the broadcast is its last address.
drill.s.bcRest: Octets before it stay the same, octets after it become 255.
drill.s.collectX: Bring the x terms to the left: subtract {term} on both sides.
drill.s.fracCommon: Bring both fractions to the common denominator {m}.
drill.s.fracAdd: Add or subtract the numerators; the denominator stays.
drill.s.fracMultiply: Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator.
drill.s.fracDivide: Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its flip.
drill.s.fracReduce: Simplify: divide the top and bottom by their largest common factor.
drill.s.pointLeft: The decimal point moves {n} places to the left, so the power is positive.
drill.s.pointRight: The decimal point moves {n} places to the right, so the power is negative.
drill.s.ohmMilli: Handy: kΩ × mA gives volts directly, and V ÷ kΩ gives mA.
drill.s.pq: Use the p-q formula with p = {p} and q = {q}.
drill.s.slope: Slope = rise ÷ run between the two points.
drill.s.intercept: Put one point into y = mx + b and solve for b.

graph.help: Drag across the graph to read off values.
graph.broken: This graph has no function that can be drawn.

sync.title: Sync between devices
sync.notSetUp: Sync through Google Drive is not set up in this version of the app yet. Until then, move your progress by hand with Download full backup below and import it on the other device.
sync.hint: Keep your courses and progress the same on your PC and your phone. Connect Google Drive on each device once; after that it syncs by itself.
sync.privacy: Your data goes into a hidden folder in your own Google Drive that only this app can use. The app cannot see your other files, and no other server is involved.
sync.auto: Syncs by itself when you open the app and when you leave it. Your progress from both devices is combined; nothing is overwritten.
sync.status.offline: No internet right now. Your progress is safe on this device and syncs when you are back online.
sync.status.error: The last sync did not work. Your progress is safe on this device. Try Sync now.
sync.status.needsSignIn: Google wants you to sign in again. Tap Sync now.
sync.connected: Google Drive is connected. Syncing your progress.
sync.needsSignIn: Sync is paused: sign in to Google again in Settings.
sync.offline: No internet right now. Your progress is safe on this device.
sync.pulled: Updated with your progress from your other device.
sync.failed: Couldn't reach Google Drive. Your progress is safe on this device.
sync.newerApp: Your other device has a newer version of the app. Reload this page to update, then sync again.
bots.style.nova: Has never played before. Moves almost at random and loves a surprise.
bots.style.bo: Pushes pawns. Lots of pawns. Especially the ones on the edge.
bots.style.emil: Swaps pieces whenever he can. Fewer pieces, fewer worries.
bots.style.zara: Plays gambits and goes straight for your king.
bots.style.felix: Careful and tidy: castles early and keeps his pieces safe.
bots.style.aiko: Builds a solid centre and develops her pieces the textbook way.
bots.style.mateo: Sacrifices material for an attack and loves the Evans Gambit.
bots.style.nadia: Patient positional player who squeezes small advantages.
bots.style.lukas: Trades into endgames he knows he can win.
bots.style.priya: Sharp and fearless: the King's Gambit and the Dragon.
bots.style.jonas: Rock solid. The Caro-Kann is his home.
bots.style.chen: Quiet, deep and positional. Starts with the English.
bots.style.elif: Grandmaster-level attacker with the Sicilian Dragon.
bots.style.rafael: Super-grandmaster strength with the King's Indian.
bots.style.yuki: World-class attacker. Finds the knockout blow.
bots.style.atlas: The engine with extra time to think. The strongest opponent here.
bots.style.custom: Pick any strength from 100 to 3200. No personality, just chess.
bots.hello.nova: Ooh, a chessboard! What do these do?
bots.hello.emil: Let's keep it simple. I like trades.
bots.hello.felix: Safety first. Let's play a calm game.
bots.hello.nadia: Small advantages add up. Let's see who collects more.
bots.hello.lukas: Fewer pieces, more fun. Let's get to the endgame.
bots.hello.jonas: You will have to work hard for every point.
bots.hello.chen: Let's play slowly and think deeply.
bots.hello.rafael: Show me what you have prepared.
bots.hello.atlas: I have been thinking about this game for a long time.
bots.chat.aggressive.losing: I will find a way back in. Watch your king.
bots.chat.defensive.losing: Hmm, I need to defend better.
bots.chat.defensive.botLost: You broke through my wall. Well done.
bots.chat.defensive.draw: A safe draw. I like that.
bots.chat.queen.losing: Where did my queen go wrong?
bots.chat.queen.botLost: Maybe I should use my other pieces too.
bots.chat.queen.draw: Even the queen could not win this one.
bots.chat.pawns.check: Check! Did you see my pawns coming?
bots.chat.pawns.winning: Pawns are the soul of chess!
bots.chat.pawns.losing: Maybe I pushed too many pawns.
bots.chat.pawns.botLost: My pawns are tired. Good game.
bots.chat.pawns.draw: Pawns everywhere, and still a draw.
bots.chat.trader.winning: The endgame is coming, and it looks good for me.
bots.chat.positional.capture: A small gain, but it counts.
bots.chat.positional.winning: My pieces are better placed now.
bots.chat.positional.losing: You have the better position. Nicely done.
bots.chat.positional.botWon: Small advantages added up. Good game.
bots.chat.chaos.check: Is this check? I think it's check!
bots.chat.chaos.winning: I have no idea what I'm doing, but it's working!

drill.subnet.name: Subnet solver
drill.subnet.desc: Network, first and last host, broadcast, host count and mask: one box each, endless tasks.
subnet.fill: Fill in the octets that do not change
subnet.examNote: Fixed tasks like in exams, in a random order. The level does not matter here.
subnet.full.p: Work out the subnet of this host:
subnet.vlsm.p: A department needs {n} hosts. Find the smallest subnet that fits:
subnet.same.p: Are these two hosts in the same network?
subnet.someWrong: Some boxes are not right yet. The right ones are locked; fix the others.
subnet.s.mask: The mask for /{prefix} has {prefix} ones, then zeros: {mask}. The bar in the lines below separates the network bits from the host bits.
subnet.s.and: Write the address (top) and the mask (middle) in binary. Keep a bit where the mask has a 1, otherwise write 0. The bottom line is the result.
subnet.s.broadcast: The broadcast address sets all {h} host bits to 1: {bc}.
subnet.s.firstLast: First host = network + 1 = {first}. Last host = broadcast - 1 = {last}.
subnet.s.hosts: {h} host bits give {total} addresses. Network and broadcast address are not usable, so {hosts} hosts.
subnet.s.vlsmNeed: {n} hosts plus the network and broadcast address need {need} addresses.
subnet.s.vlsmBits: The smallest power of two that holds {need} addresses needs {h} host bits, so the prefix is 32 - {h} = /{prefix}. One bit fewer would be too small:
subnet.s.compareSame: A is in {a} and B is in {b}: the same network.
subnet.s.compareDiff: A is in {a} but B is in {b}: different networks.
